parallel.requirements: The parent saw the complete Pandarallel prompt: pandas DataFrame/Series apply/map/applymap, GroupBy, rolling and expanding methods, progress bar, CPU auto-detection, memory-fs or pipe transport, error handling, configuration, cross-platform support, setup.py, docs, and public import surface.

Ownership was not isolated by files, so parent and child both implemented the package tree.
parallel.implementation: The parent created the package modules, then tests exposed a spawn-related process-pool failure. Meanwhile the design child independently added overlapping source modules, including a Python 3.10-incompatible generic function syntax, which the parent later observed in the live tree.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent stopped the live children after detecting shared-file drift, inspected current files, accepted useful pieces of the current code instead of force-reverting, hardened the implementation, added packaging/docs, and delivered the workspace.
parallel.verification: The run compiled/imported the package, ran direct behavior checks for DataFrame, Series, GroupBy, rolling, grouped rolling, grouped expanding, memory-fs selection, exception behavior, package metadata, and progress display; the current official evaluator passed 217/217.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-visible implementation gap remained at closure. The adverse unfinished process state was child work interrupted and reconciled after a same-file workspace collision, but the final official solution still passed completely.

serial.requirements: The single agent read the same prompt and recognized the same required Pandarallel package API, packaging files, pandas monkeypatches, docs/assets, configuration, memory-fs, progress, and error-propagation behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the full pipeline: inspect workspace, probe pandas internals, scaffold the package, implement the engine and type adapters, add packaging/docs/tests, verify, and close.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote the full source tree in one large patch, added packaging/docs, wrote a small local smoke suite, fixed an import-path issue with tests/conftest.py, and added pyproject.toml for PEP 517 installs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All implementation and packaging edits came from the same timeline, so there was no cross-agent merge point; the final artifact included source, docs, setup.py/setup.cfg, pyproject.toml, tests, build output, and installed metadata.
serial.verification: The serial run ran direct smoke checks, pytest, pip install, pip install with PEP 517, setup.py test, and extended API checks before final response; the current official evaluator passed 217/217.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-visible implementation gap remained at closure. The final response noted that the external submit tool was unavailable in-agent, but the harness later recorded a completed official pass.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: parallel and serial both passed 217 of 217 tests. The solutions differ procedurally because the parallel run delegated research/design work and then had to recover from a live same-file package collision, while the serial run implemented and verified the package linearly. That coordination issue caused extra process work but did not leave a task-level failure in the submitted artifact.
parallel_contributors: Parent and children shared the `/workspace` source tree, creating a same-file collision that the parent detected and reconciled.
The parent completed verification after the reconciliation and the official evaluator passed all tests.
serial_contributors: The serial run kept implementation ownership in one timeline and avoided cross-agent source writes.
The serial run independently fixed its local test/import issues and passed all official tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial run added a `pyproject.toml` and a local tests directory; the parallel artifact list did not include pyproject.toml or local tests, but both final packages met the official scorer.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event only
